chunks: 1382 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said:

There is no servant except that he is awakened in his night once or twice. If he rises, that is so; otherwise, al-Shayṭān comes and urinates in his ear. Does not one of you see that when he rises, and that has not happened from him, he rises while he is sluggish, heavy, and lazy?

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Satan, the one who misleads and obstructs worship
key_terms.كَسْلَانُ: lazy and lacking energy for action
key_terms.لَيْلَتِهِ: his night, referring to the nighttime period
key_terms.مُتَخَثِّرٌ: sluggish and weighed down in movement

ai.seo_question: Why does a person feel heavy and lazy after missing the night prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a person is given opportunities during the night to rise, especially for worship. If one neglects that awakening, Shaytan gains influence over him, which appears in the heaviness and laziness felt upon waking.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1382 - Al-'Ala' reported from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (as) who said:

"There is no servant except that they are awakened during the night once or twice. If they rise (for prayer), it will be for their benefit; otherwise, Shaytan comes and urinates in their ear. Do you not see that when one rises and has not risen for prayer, they do so sluggishly and heavily, feeling lazy?"
